biologia-molecular.resumen: Molecular Biology is a key tool for precision diagnosis: it impacts prognosis and therapeutic selection. Our service integrates validated molecular techniques in close correlation with anatomopathological findings, ensuring reliable results aligned with current scientific standards.

destacados.detalle: The BenchMark ULTRA is the most innovative and fully automated in situ hybridization slide staining system from Roche Tissue Diagnostics. Individual sliding drawers for one-piece workflow and a menu of over 250 ready-to-use assays.
Performed under stable conditions, with identical antisera and computerized controls.
Improved quality of life and increased chances in pregnancy management.

inmunohistoquimica.resumen: An essential tool for modern anatomic pathology: tumor typing, evaluation of prognostic and predictive factors — providing decisive information for classification and clinical decisions. We use standardized techniques with automated protocols on Ventana's BenchMark Ultra platform, with monoclonal and polyclonal antibodies and rigorous quality controls.

paneles.detalle: Key markers in precision oncology. Provides essential information for therapeutic selection.
CD3 · CD4 · CD8 · CD16 · CD20 · CD45 · CD56 · CD68 · CD138
Hormone receptors (Estrogen and Progesterone) · Her2-Neu · Ki-67 · Proteins 5/6 · 8/18 · P-53
Classification of lymphoid and myeloid neoplasms.
Oriented to identifying the primary tumor site.

tecnicas-alta-complejidad.resumen: Complementary methods to the anatomopathological diagnosis that expand the resolution, sensitivity, and precision of the report in complex pathologies.

sub.descripcion: A rapid diagnostic method that provides multiple parameters from cells and particles from liquid samples or fresh solid tissue. Invaluable in Hematopathology: diagnosis, classification, and determination of prognostic factors in lymphoproliferative entities.
envio: Fresh material: tissue biopsies refrigerated with ice (do not freeze). Send same day.
Peripheral blood and fluids: EDTA tube at room temperature (do not refrigerate). Send same day.

sub.descripcion: Technique using fluorescent markers to identify molecules on the cell surface. Performed on fresh tissue.
envio: Fresh material: tissue biopsies refrigerated with ice (do not freeze). Send same day.

sub.descripcion: Technique that provides high-resolution images of cellular ultrastructure. Used as a complementary method to anatomopathological diagnosis.

histopatologia.resumen: Processing and diagnosis of biopsies and surgical specimens with routine stains and special techniques. Average turnaround: 6 business days for biopsy and 9 business days for biopsy with immunohistochemistry.

citologia.resumen: Cervicovaginal screening (Pap smear) with specialized reading and fast delivery — 3 business days on average — and evaluation of samples obtained by fine-needle aspiration (FNA) from solid organs.

complementarios.detalle: Rapid diagnosis during surgery to define immediate management of the specimen.
Wide battery of complementary stains (PAS, Trichrome, Reticulin, Ziehl-Neelsen, Giemsa, among others) for tissue characterization.
Review of cases from other centers, with slide re-interpretation and additional studies when appropriate.
Ongoing dialogue with treating physicians to correlate morphological findings with clinical context and guide therapeutic decisions.

hero.title: We're with you every step.
hero.description: A biopsy or cytology request can raise questions. Here you'll find clear information on what each study is, how to prepare, and how to pick up your report.

bloques.title: What is a biopsy?
bloques.text: It's the microscopic study of a tissue or cell sample obtained by a physician. Our pathologists analyze it to establish an accurate diagnosis that guides treatment.

bloques.title: How long does the report take?
bloques.text: Turnaround varies by study type: Pap smear 3 business days, biopsy 6 business days, immunohistochemistry 7 business days, and biopsy with IHC 9 business days. More complex studies (molecular biology, special techniques) may require additional time.

bloques.title: How do I pick up my report?
bloques.text: The report is delivered to your referring physician; you can also pick it up in person with your ID or request it by email with proof of identity.

bloques.title: Where are we?
bloques.text: Concepción Arenal 3732, Buenos Aires. Open Monday to Friday from 8:00 to 20:00.

portal.title: Your report, available.
portal.description: The original report is sent directly to your referring physician. You can also pick up a copy at our office, request it by email with proof of identity, or check by phone.
portal.inValue: Concepción Arenal 3732, Buenos Aires · Mon–Fri 08:00 to 20:00

pacientes.faqFooter: Didn't find what you were looking for?

faqs.q: Do I need an appointment to drop off a sample?
faqs.a: No appointment needed. You can come Monday to Friday from 8:00 to 20:00. For surgical specimens or material with special requirements, we coordinate pickup by phone.

faqs.q: What should I bring on the day of the sample?
faqs.a: Yes: the original medical order, your ID, and your health insurance credential if applicable. If you have related prior studies, bring them too.
The original report is sent to your referring physician. You can pick up a copy with your ID, request it by email, or check by phone.

faqs.q: Do you work with my insurer?
faqs.a: We work with the main insurers, HMOs, and hospitals in the country. See the full list in the Insurance section or call us to confirm your coverage.

faqs.q: What if my doctor requests a second opinion?
faqs.a: We accept consultations and second opinions on material already processed at another laboratory. Bring the paraffin blocks and original slides along with the previous report.

faqs.q: Can I request the same report years later?
faqs.a: Yes. We keep slides and paraffin blocks for the periods required by current regulations. You can request a copy of the report or the original material with proof of identity.

faqs.q: How do you protect my data?
faqs.a: We operate under Law 25.326 on Personal Data Protection. Your clinical information is confidential and only shared with you and your treating physician.
